cases.name: foreign
cases.note: An empty library written by Python's sqlite3 in its own style: quoted identifiers, lower-case types, table constraints, NOT NULL on the primary keys.

cases.name: foreign-older
cases.note: Only v1, sync-reconciliation and history-record-index are recorded and created: a reader applies the other two migrations.

cases.name: foreign-trigger
cases.note: A trigger the migrations do not create.

cases.name: foreign-view
cases.note: A view the migrations do not create.

cases.name: foreign-extra-table
cases.note: A table the migrations do not create.

cases.name: foreign-missing-column
cases.note: records has no dirty column.

cases.name: foreign-nullable-column
cases.note: records.kind may be NULL.

cases.name: foreign-unknown-migration
cases.note: grdb_migrations lists a migration this version does not know: written by a newer version.

cases.name: foreign-migration-objects-missing
cases.note: server-versions is recorded but its table was never created.

cases.name: foreign-migrations-out-of-order
cases.note: history-checkpoints is recorded without the migrations before it.

cases.name: foreign-wal
cases.note: File format versions 2 and 2 (write-ahead logging): not a one-file snapshot.

cases.name: foreign-small-pages
cases.note: The same library on 512-byte pages: the schema table is a b-tree with interior pages, which a reader that counts its rows by reading the pages must walk.

cases.name: foreign-implicit-parent-key
cases.note: outbox.record references records without naming a column, which means the parent's primary key: the same key as references records (id).

cases.name: foreign-virtual-table
cases.note: An FTS5 virtual table and its shadow tables. Connecting a virtual table runs the module's code, so it is refused from the schema table, before quick_check or any pragma.

cases.name: foreign-generated-column
cases.note: records has a generated column that PRAGMA table_info leaves out and table_xinfo lists (hidden 2 or 3).

cases.name: foreign-check-constraint
cases.note: records.revision has a CHECK constraint, which no pragma lists.

cases.name: foreign-collate
cases.note: records.kind compares as NOCASE.

cases.name: foreign-foreign-key-action
cases.note: outbox.record deletes the row with its record (ON DELETE CASCADE).

cases.name: foreign-deferred-foreign-key
cases.note: outbox.record is DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED.

cases.name: foreign-on-conflict-replace
cases.note: outbox.record is UNIQUE ON CONFLICT REPLACE.

cases.name: foreign-without-rowid
cases.note: settings is a WITHOUT ROWID table.

cases.name: foreign-strict
cases.note: settings is a STRICT table.

cases.name: foreign-no-autoincrement
cases.note: history.id is not AUTOINCREMENT, so its numbers can be used again.

comparison: Tables, columns (name, declared type in upper case, NOT NULL, default without outer parentheses, primary key position), indexes (CREATE INDEX name, uniqueness, partial, key columns), foreign keys (parent table, columns, ON UPDATE, ON DELETE, MATCH; a key that names no parent column means the parent's primary key) and whether the table is AUTOINCREMENT are compared; the text of CREATE statements is not. A primary key column counts as NOT NULL. grdb_migrations is compared by its identifier column only. sqlite_sequence is ignored. Triggers, views, virtual tables, generated or hidden columns, WITHOUT ROWID and STRICT tables, any statement that contains the word CHECK, COLLATE, CONFLICT, DEFERRABLE, GENERATED, AS or VIRTUAL outside quotes and comments, and any other table or index are refused.
purpose: The structure of the library database after each migration (protocol/archive.md, Database), and databases written by something other than GRDB that a reader accepts or refuses before it opens them. See README.md in this folder.
